symptom: `create page Wd.P (…) { container c (Visible: roles (Administration.Administrator)) {…} }` passed `mxcli check --references` and `exec`; `mx check` then reported CE0149 "Visibility needs to be updated, reselect roles in properties". A role of the page's own module, viewable or not, was clean.
file: mdl/executor/validate_visible_roles_module.go ValidateVisibleRolesModule (MDL-GRANT04), called from validate_program.go next to ValidateGrantRoles. Tests: validate_visible_roles_module_test.go; fixtures mdl-examples/bug-tests/visible-roles-cross-module(.fail).mdl
cause: validate_grant_refs.go (widgetVisibleRoles) only checks that each role EXISTS; nothing compared the role's module with the document's. MDL-GRANT01 already did that for document grants (CE0148) and was never extended to a widget's role list, the same mistake one property over.
insight: **When a rule exists for one place a Mendix reference list is stored (document grants: CE0148), ask for every other place that stores the same kind of list before calling it done: the same-module restriction is a property of how Mendix stores module roles, not of GRANT.** Measured on MxBuild 11.16.1, one `mx check -j` over 17 documents: container, dynamic text, layout-grid row, navigation-list item, snippet container, layout container, tab page and a widget inserted by alter page are each CE0149 for a foreign role (Administration.Administrator or a role of a user-created module) and clean for an own-module one; an own+foreign list is CE0149; viewing access is irrelevant. The report's first guess was page access; the measurement said module only. Tab pages were unreachable until the separate MDL-WIDGET44 false refusal of `Visible: roles` on a tab page was fixed. Case-insensitive module compare (unmeasured whether Mendix distinguishes) and unqualified roles skipped, so a miss rather than a false report. Sweep of every .mdl in the repo: 0 hits, but only 8 scripts mention `roles (` and one uses Visible: roles (an own-module role), so the sweep is weak evidence here; the measurement is the evidence. Control: stubbing the rule fails all 11 positive cases, the one-violation test and the ValidateProgram wiring test; the positive-control script builds with 0 errors on MxBuild.
